category_title: Highly verbal preschoolers who talk out of turn during group activities
minimal_context: Sybil is participating in a large group circle time discussion where the class is sharing weekend stories.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Welcome to circle time, everyone. Today we are going to share our favorite things we did over the weekend. Who would like to go first?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I went to the zoo with my family and we saw the monkeys and they were swinging everywhere and making funny noises!

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Thank you for sharing. Let's see what Sarah did.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: And after the monkeys we saw the lions but they were just sleeping in the sun, so we went to get pretzels!

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Sarah, it is your turn to speak now.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I like pretzels with cheese! Sarah, did you get pretzels too? My dad said we can go back next week and see the elephants!

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Welcome to circle time, everyone. Today we are going to share our favorite things we did over the weekend. Who would like to go first?

STUDENT: I went to the zoo with my family and we saw the monkeys and they were swinging everywhere and making funny noises!

TUTOR: Thank you for sharing. Let's see what Sarah did.

STUDENT: And after the monkeys we saw the lions but they were just sleeping in the sun, so we went to get pretzels!

TUTOR: Sarah, it is your turn to speak now.

STUDENT: I like pretzels with cheese! Sarah, did you get pretzels too? My dad said we can go back next week and see the elephants!

task.content: Listen and learn from friends and adults in the classroom, and allow other children time to share.
task.learning_goal: Decrease talking out of turn to less than 30% of the specified intervals.

context.environment: Large group circle time in the preschool classroom.
context.materials: Pictures to remind Sybil to raise her hand before speaking and wait her turn to talk.
context.social_setting: Group activities with peers and adults.

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: During conversations with peers and adults when she wants to share stories.
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Sybil does not raise her hand or signal the need to speak before talking; talks over a friend or adult; and does not pause to hear her friend’s or adult’s response.

behavior_patterns.condition: During group activities in the classroom.
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Talking out of turn as much as 80% of the time, talking so much that the other children do not have time to share.
